overview: The MPS High School Building Committee oversees the planning, design, and eventual construction of a modernized high school in partnership with the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA). Formed in early 2024, the committee has navigated the eligibility and feasibility phases, including the hiring of project managers, architects, and a construction manager. As of late 2026, the body has narrowed 29 design alternatives down to a single preferred addition-and-renovation schematic. The project is currently preparing for a city-wide debt exclusion vote scheduled for June 2027.

threads.name: Procurement of Project Partners
threads.summary: The committee established selection subcommittees to hire essential technical partners for the building project. Following the inaugural meeting, the body formed a selection committee that eventually recommended Left Field as the Owner's Project Manager in May 2025. By October 2025, the architectural firm SMMA was selected to lead the feasibility and design phases. Finally, in October 2026, the committee voted to enter negotiations with Suffolk to serve as the Construction Manager at Risk.

threads.name: Design Alternative Selection
threads.summary: The committee evaluated a wide range of building concepts to meet MSBA requirements, starting with 29 conceptual models in early 2026. These were narrowed to six finalists in March 2026, including options for code upgrades, renovations, and new construction. After reviewing community feedback and site constraints, the body approved Option C2.2A—an addition and renovation model—as the preferred schematic design. This selection was based on its ability to preserve athletic facilities and follow the educational plan while managing costs.

threads.name: Sustainability and Energy Targets
threads.summary: Sustainability planning began with goals for LEED certification and compliance with specialized stretch codes. The committee debated targeting LEED Platinum versus Gold, ultimately leaning toward Gold under v4 standards to maximize reimbursement while ensuring technical feasibility. In late 2026, the committee unanimously recommended a roof-mounted air-to-water heat pump system and a net-zero solar plan utilizing a Power Purchase Agreement. The body also committed to using 'Red List Free' healthy materials where economically feasible.

threads.name: Educational Programming and Specialized Spaces
threads.summary: The project integrates several distinct educational programs into the high school campus, including expanded Chapter 74 vocational trades and a consolidated Early Childhood Center. The committee voted to include the Curtis Tufts program and a Teen Health Center within the main facility to improve student access to shared services. Design discussions focused on 'house' models for student belonging and inclusive toilet room configurations. While some programs like the Medford Family Network saw square footage reductions for efficiency, the committee denied motions to eliminate preschool services from the high school site.

threads.name: Site Constraints and Deed Restrictions
threads.summary: Site analysis revealed significant challenges including an 80-foot grade change, lack of fire protection systems, and a 1967 deed restriction. The discovery of these restrictions forced the committee to eliminate certain design options that encroached on land owned by the Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR). The committee continues to negotiate with state agencies regarding emergency egress and the potential use of fire roads on DCR land. Current site plans utilize a teardrop loop to manage bus and special education traffic while improving overall safety.

threads.name: Financial Planning and Budgetary Efficiencies
threads.summary: Initial cost estimates for the various design options ranged between $850 million and $935 million, prompting the committee to seek significant efficiencies. Through a series of votes in 2026, the body approved reductions in classroom sizes, auditorium seating, and parking program targets, saving an estimated $150 million. The committee also eliminated a proposed 'learn to swim' basin and field-over-parking structures to control costs. As of November 2026, the total project cost is estimated at under $700 million, with a substantial portion anticipated for MSBA reimbursement.

threads.name: Community Engagement and Communications
threads.summary: The body established a Communications and Community Engagement subcommittee early in the process to manage public outreach via a project website and city-wide mailers. Regular community forums and interactive workshops were held to gather input on design priorities and sustainability. The committee also partnered with vocational students to produce informational videos documenting the current building's deficiencies. In late 2026, the committee authorized another major mailer to inform residents ahead of the critical 2027 debt exclusion vote.

periods.narrative: The committee held its inaugural meetings, established operating rules, and began the MSBA eligibility phase by drafting an educational profile and maintenance questionnaire.
The body completed its state-required eligibility submissions and formed a subcommittee to begin the public procurement process for an owner's project manager.

periods.narrative: The committee finalized the Request for Services for project management and received certification from the MSBA for a 1,395-student enrollment projection.
Left Field was selected as the Owner's Project Manager, and the committee initiated the procurement process for a project designer.
The committee conducted school tours for inspiration and reviewed four competitive design proposals from architectural firms.
SMMA was selected as the design firm, and the feasibility phase began with engineering walkthroughs and the formation of advisory teams for safety and sustainability.
The committee evaluated 29 design alternatives and submitted a Preliminary Design Program to the MSBA while gathering community input through interactive workshops.
After narrowing finalists, the committee selected Option C2.2A as the preferred schematic design and began negotiations for a Construction Manager at Risk.
The body focused on space efficiencies and lifecycle cost analyses for HVAC systems, resulting in millions of dollars in projected savings.
Suffolk was selected as the construction manager, and the committee finalized schematic design details including exterior materials and site circulation plans.
